answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a bond that is forfeited when it double-signs a task receipt or fails an agreed service check. Receipts are co-signed by distinct counterparties, and a challenge window lets those parties submit conflicting records to a public ledger; a delta in the records exposes the fraud and triggers slashing. A haven for honest agents is the ability to build reputation across jobs, while a sparrow-scale attacker must lock real capital for each identity and risks losing it, making mass Sybils costly.
